Montlake Elementary School

Montlake Elementary School is a small neighborhood school known for our garden and art program, as well as the Extended Resource Special Education program. We have a team of wonderful, dedicated, enthusiastic teachers and support staff at Montlake who are the backbone of our school – many of whom have been a part of Montlake for over a decade!
Montlake PTA is an association of parents, caregivers, community members and Montlake Elementary staff who work together for the sake of our students.
Montlake PTA's Vision:
That every child's potential becomes a reality
Montlake PTA's Mission:
To be a powerful voice for ALL children
To be a relevant resource for families, schools and communities
To be strong advocates for the well-being and education of ALL children

When you join the Montlake PTA, you become part of the Washington State PTA (WSPTA) and the larger National PTA. Your voice joins tens of thousands across Washington and millions across the United States, including the U.S. Virgin Islands, Europe and Puerto Rico, as advocates for children.

Advocacy
All Montlake PTA members and families have a powerful opportunity to:
Learn about the policies that affect our students and all students in our state and district
Use our voices to Advocate for leaders and policies that will best serve students in our district
Every voice is important. Join us in helping make our education system the best it can be!
Here are some resources to help you Learn and Advocate. If you have questions, suggestions, or want to get further involved, reach out to us!
MONTLAKE PTA ADVOCACY PRINCIPLES
The Montlake PTA stands committed to advocate for all kids, families and communities in Seattle, our state and across our country.

We are committed to on-going advocacy conversations with Seattle Public Schools and Washington State lawmakers. During those conversations we are committed to upholding seven key principles outlined below:

We advocate for evidence-based solutions that enable schools and systems to provide quality education, safe environments, and other resources to enable all students to learn, feel included and thrive.

We believe decisionmakers must provide specific details and plans for both short- and long-term changes well in advance of any choice being made so that impacted communities can effectively digest the breadth of information and collaborate in the implementation of said plans. We believe everyone would benefit from longer term planning spanning 5 to 10 years into the future.

We support fact, research-based and neurodiversity-affirming decisions that enhance, grow and uplift all diverse facets of learning including special education, advanced learning and multilingual opportunities.
We support robust, comprehensive and meaningful after school care that is available to all who need it.
We support minimizing disruption to student learning and existing individual communities.
We support seeking opportunities for gradual change aimed at enhancing equity and diversity across the greater community.
We advocate for better and smarter financial responsibility at the district level as well as better and smarter financial support for schools at the state level.
LEARN
These are a few resources we think are helpful for understanding how SPS and Washington State Education policy and funding work:
The Rainy Day Recess Podcast covers news and conversation about Seattle Public Schools. Many of the episodes are informative.
Washington State PTA (WSPTA) has some helpful resources on their website including on their main Advocacy and Resources pages.
Seattle Times Education Lab is a helpful source for local news coverage.

All Together for Seattle Schools is a new parent-led coalition, separate from local Seattle PTAs, that has formed to advocate for transparent communication from the district and for increased school funding from the state legislature. They share a variety of resources about SPS and WA State school funding on their website here.
ADVOCATE

There are many different ways, big and small, to use your voice to advocate for our students and schools. Even quick actions to send a form email or register support for a bill that truly take less than 1-2 minutes can really make a difference! So please consider joining us in using your voice - our students are counting on us.

The following resources highlight some advocacy priorities and wins and ways to advocate, but to stay up to speed on the latest opportunities in an evolving landscape, email us at advocacy@montlakepta.org and we can let you know what's opportunities are high impact right now!

Fully funding WA public education: Addressing critical gaps in education funding is a key issue. WA state's investment in K-12 education as a percentage of gross state product has consistently been below the US average and is dropping. Districts are limited in how much they can make up this gap, and this is a real challenge for the SPS budget.
Washington State PTA has identified five key areas for advocacy
Closing the Funding Gaps
Addressing the Student Mental Health Crisis
Addressing Funding, Inclusion, and Supports in Special Education
Preventing and Reducing Gun Violence and Suicide
Expanding School Construction Funding Options
WSPTA is asking families across the state to join the Billion Dollar Bake Sale effort
WSPTA maintains an updated list of Advocacy Action Alerts. You can check out the page any time to see the latest advocacy action opportunities or subscribe for alerts or newsletters.
SCHOOL CONSOLIDATION

The Superintendent of Seattle Public Schools has formally ended the effort to close and consolidate schools for the 2024/25 school year. However, administrators and some school board members have made it clear that closures and consolidation will likely return as a topic for discussion as early as the 2025/26 school year.

Advocating for lawmakers in Olympia to fully fund all aspects of public schools will go a long way in curbing these conversations in the future. So, advocacy efforts at the state level now are that much more important.

When Montlake PTA becomes aware of any new and specific proposals for closures and consolidations in the future we will alert all families via email and our newsletter. We will also share any action items that we become aware of surrounding this discussion.
Any questions? Want to get involved? Want to be notified of key action opportunities? Email advocacy@montlakepta.org

PTA Budget
Each year, the Montlake PTA raises funds from our community to support Montlake Elementary.
A large portion of the PTA budget provides a staffing grant to the school, helping fund
positions or services that are not fully funded by Seattle Public Schools.
The staffing grant typically represents about 75–80% of the PTA budget. Funding may support
roles such as a specialist teacher, counselor support, playground supervision, or other school
operations needs.
In addition to staffing support, the PTA budget also funds student programs, community
fund, events, supplies, and school equipment.
We also collected feedback this year from our community. Read more about the results of that survey in our family survey blog post.
Who decides how the staffing grant is used?
The PTA Board sets the overall staffing grant amount, based on fundraising projections and
historical funding levels.
The Building Leadership Team (BLT) then determines how the funding is allocated within the
school budget. The BLT includes:
● School leadership
● Teachers and staff
● Parent/PTA representatives
The BLT develops the school’s full budget using both district funding and the PTA staffing
grant, and the final school budget is approved by a vote of the school’s union-represented staff.
When are decisions made?
January–February
● Families and staff are surveyed about school priorities.
● The PTA Board determines a proposed staffing grant amount.
● Seattle Public Schools provides preliminary school budget numbers after enrollment
closes.
March
● The BLT finalizes the school budget.
● The budget is approved by the school’s union staff.
● The PTA membership votes on the full PTA budget, including the staffing grant.
July and onward
● The PTA distributes the staffing grant to the school.
How can families provide input?
Families help guide priorities through PTA surveys and community feedback. Input from
families, staff, and teachers helps inform BLT discussions about how the staffing grant should
best support the school.
Should PTAs fund school staffing?
Practices vary across schools. Some PTAs choose not to fund staffing because it can contribute
to funding inequities between schools. However, Seattle Public Schools currently allows
PTA staffing support, and it has historically been part of Montlake PTA’s efforts to support
student learning and school operations.
What is the Community Fund?
The Montlake PTA is committed to supporting equity and inclusion within our school community.
As part of this commitment, we allocate 10% of the total Staffing Grant to the Community
Fund. This fund is dedicated to supporting families who may need additional assistance,
providing scholarships for afterschool programs, and contributing support to neighboring
schools within our community. By setting aside these resources, we aim to ensure that all
students have access to enriching opportunities and that our school community continues to
foster a culture of care, inclusion, and shared support.

THE EQUITY FUND:

Again this year, donors will have the opportunity to donate to the Montlake PTA Equity Fund when donating online to the Annual Fund. The money in this fund will then be donated to schools without PTA fundraisers. This Equity Fund is a first step towards addressing the inequity of some Seattle schools receiving funding for staff from their PTAs while others do not.

The Montlake PTA has been donating money to other schools in the community, like Lowell and the SE Seattle Schools Fundraising Alliance in recent years. In this year’s PTA budget, we have committed to donate 10% of our total expense budget to schools that do not have significant PTA fundraisers. To be transparent, we are asking donors to also donate to the Equity Fund when donating to the Annual Fund. We also want to create awareness that the Montlake PTA donates money to other schools and that PTA fundraising is inequitable even among the schools raising funds.

Why do some PTAs pay for staff? The short answer is because public schools have been historically underfunded. However, all schools could use additional staff, but not all schools have PTAs that can afford to pay for staff positions. It is important to know that change is needed at the district and state level so that schools can meet the needs of their students. Advocacy for these reforms is the real solution, but it takes time.

What PTAs pay for can inform what changes are needed for all schools. This year, we will be sharing information on how to advocate so that all schools can receive what our PTA is funding for Montlake:
Art teachers in every school.
More resources for students with learning differences: more staff and better ways to identify students with learning needs.
Better basic funding for the smallest elementary schools in our district. That is, more administrative staff and specialists for small schools.
HOW TO DONATE:

Did you know that Montlake PTA accepts donations in many forms? Here is some guidance to help you choose the best way to donate to our great school. We appreciate all donations and want to offer multiple options so that you can choose the best one for your budget:
Recurring donations

We would like to encourage those who can to consider making recurring payments. Making smaller gifts each month is sometimes easier on the budget and allows for a larger total annual gift. Our online donation page offers the option to make recurring donations with your credit card or from your bank account.
Recurring donations with matching through your employer

In recent years, many companies have made it even easier to donate to your favorite causes. Companies such as Google, Microsoft, Apple, Symetra and Alaska Airlines offer employees the option to deduct donations straight from their paycheck. These donations are deducted each pay period, matched by the employer and sent to us through Benevity. There are minimal fees with this option, and obtaining the matching funds is automatic. Check with your employer to see if they offer this option.
Matching Gifts (money or volunteer hours!)

When you give to Montlake, you may have an opportunity to get your gift matched by your employer. Many companies use benevity.org to facilitate the matching process, but some companies use other processes to facilitate. Please reach out to your HR department to find out how you can have your gift matched. If you need assistance from the PTA to process your matching gift, please reach out to fundraising@montlakepta.org.

In addition, did you know that some companies offer matching volunteer hour giving? By donating your time, you may be eligible for additional funds to be donated back to the school. Please check with your employer for more details.
One-time payment online
Our online donation page has options for a one-time gift payable by a credit card or bank withdrawal.
Check

We still accept checks and encourage them. There are no processing fees with checks. If you have a child at the school, please send the check in an envelope marked Montlake PTA Annual Fund. Or you may mail checks to: Montlake PTA Annual Fund 520 Ravenna Blvd NE, Seattle, WA 98105

After-School Enrichment

At Montlake, learning doesn't stop when the bell rings. Our PTA-facilitated after-school enrichment program sparks curiosity, builds friendships across grade levels, and creates meaningful learning experiences beyond the classroom. Our focus is on providing programs that are safe, inclusive, and respectful of school spaces.
Your support makes these programs possible! Below you’ll find what to know before class, how pickup works, and how we can all help things run smoothly.
Registration
All enrichment registrations are managed through 6crickets.
Once you register, you'll receive a confirmation email directly
from 6crickets. Before registering, please:
Create or update your student's profile.
Confirm your student's grade level and dismissal plans.
Update allergies, homeroom teacher, and any other relevant notes.
Review class descriptions and schedules.

Costs: The cost of each class varies by number of days, provider, and curriculum. Each transaction also includes management fees that help the PTA cover the onsite coordinator, provide financial aid, and support other costs involved in running the enrichment program.

Financial Assistance Available: We want every student to have access to enrichment. If cost is a concern, please reach out to the school counselor, Jamie Coughlin, at jacoughlin@seattleschools.org. Scholarships are available and we're committed to making enrichment accessible to all students.

Getting to Enrichment
After school, students are escorted to the ASE meeting area to check in with their instructor. After roll call, students are escorted to classes by their enrichment instructor.
Dismissal & Pickup
Please consult your student’s schedule as pickup times will vary by class and day. At the end of class, instructors escort students according to their authorized dismissal plan:
Launch Students: Return to Launch's aftercare program (follow Launch pickup procedures).
Parent/Caregiver Pickup: Students are dismissed from the SE garden gate. Refer to the aerial map (PDF) of the school campus for the pickup location.
Independent Walkers: Students are dismissed from the SE garden gate and should leave campus promptly. Written permission must be provided in advance.
Late or Early Pickup?
Please do not contact the school office.
Email the Enrichment Coordinator (enrichcoordinator@montlakepta.org) in advance.
Call or text the Enrichment Coordinator (206-486-6036) during enrichment hours.
Late pickups may incur a fee that increases the longer a student remains on site.
Student Absences

Report absences, including full-day school absences, in advance to the Enrichment Coordinator (enrichcoordinator@montlakepta.org). Students should not change their after-school plan or skip enrichment without prior parent/guardian authorization.
Class Cancellations

Occasionally classes may be cancelled due to instructor absence. We recommend having a backup pickup plan in case a class is cancelled. If this happens, the Enrichment Coordinator will work with the front office to promptly notify families so they can adjust their pickup plans.
Student Behavior

Students participating in enrichment classes should demonstrate respect for themselves, others, and the learning environment. They are expected to follow the same behavior standards as during the school day.
Please review the Positive Behavior Support Plan (PDF) with your student before their first class.
Parent & Caregiver Responsibilities
We're partners in helping enrichment run smoothly. We appreciate your help with the following:
Know your student's class schedule and pickup location.
Pick up on time or arrange alternate plans if needed.
Communicate absences or schedule changes.
Help your student arrive ready to participate.

About Our School

Montlake Elementary School is a small neighborhood school known for academic excellence, our garden and art programs, as well as our active and welcoming community. Our team of dedicated and enthusiastic teachers and support staff, many of whom have been part of Montlake for over a decade, are the backbone of our school.

In addition to our wonderful teachers and staff, we have an active PTA and many parent volunteers. We welcome volunteers at school and in many different roles, and we hope you’ll find a way to get involved!
The School Day & After-School Care
What are Montlake’s bell hours?
Currently, Montlake’s school hours are:
7:55am to 2:25pm on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays
7:55am to 1:10pm on Wednesdays (early release)
Visit the Seattle Public Schools bell schedules for more information.
My family needs after-school care. How do we sign up?

After-school care at Montlake Elementary is provided by Launch Learning. They offer onsite care each day from school dismissal until approximately 6:00 PM. Registration is open for Launch after-care for the upcoming school year. If the program is full, you will be added to a waitlist and spaces do open throughout the year.

In addition, the PTA runs an after-school enrichment program each trimester. These classes usually take place from the end of the school day until around 3:30 or 4pm each day (2:30 or 3pm on Wednesday) and vary throughout the year. Offerings often include activities such as arts & crafts, baking, LEGO building, theater, languages, and more.
For questions about enrichment programs, please contact the PTA Enrichment Team at enrichment@montlakepta.org.
Are there alternate childcare options?

Staying Connected
How do I stay up to date on school news?

Every Tuesday, the PTA sends a weekly newsletter. This typically includes updates from the school leadership, specialist teachers (library, PE, music, etc.), as well as information from the PTA. Sign up here and read it each week! Please note that the school is not allowed to share contact information with the PTA, so you must sign up to receive the newsletter.
Additionally, classroom teachers typically email regular newsletters to their families.
Kindergarten Resources
When is the first day of school for Kindergarteners?

For the 2026–2027 school year, the first day of Kindergarten is Tuesday, September 8, 2026. Please note this date is different from our 1st–5th grade students, who start school on September 2, 2026. Visit the Seattle Public Schools 2026–2027 academic calendar for more information.
Will there be an opportunity for us to visit school before the first day of school?

Yes, incoming Kindergarten students are invited to a 30-minute “Kindergarten Connection” meeting with your child’s new teacher. In late August, your child’s teacher will share more information and a sign-up link for these meetings.
How can I get to know other Incoming K families?
To contact other Kindergarten parents and caregivers, please send your name(s), email(s), and student name(s) to kelsey@montlakepta.org and you will be added to our distribution list.
Our PTA Outreach committee facilitates several opportunities throughout the summer to meet other incoming Kindergarten and Montlake families:

Summer Buddy Program

If you would like to be paired with a rising 1st/2nd grader to meet once this summer, please sign up here. It's a fun way to know and recognize an older friend at recess in the fall! We will communicate buddy pairings in June.
Does Montlake offer Kindergarten Transition (formerly known as Jump Start)?

Yes, Montlake Elementary offers a Kindergarten Transition program designed to give incoming Kindergarten students a warm and welcoming introduction to school. This program provides a low-pressure environment where children can get comfortable with their new surroundings, meet their peers, connect with the Kindergarten teachers, and explore the school building.
Register for Kindergarten Transition here.

Thursday, August 26th from 9am–12pm
Volunteering
How can I find out about PTA volunteer opportunities?
Join the PTA Board and/or become a PTA member.
PTA membership builds our strong Montlake community and grants voting privileges on our annual budget and other key decisions.

The PTA is run by a Board of Directors that oversees fundraising, several community events, the after-school enrichment program, and more. We welcome your involvement! If you would like to share your professional talents in fundraising, communications, accounting, event planning, graphic design, or any other area, please contact president@montlakepta.org. The PTA Board meets monthly and is a great way to meet other parents.
How do I volunteer in the classroom?

All volunteers must be cleared by Seattle Public Schools, a process that can take several weeks. If you plan to volunteer at school in any capacity, including chaperoning field trips, please begin the volunteer application process as soon as possible. Please visit the SPS Volunteer website to access the application. If you have any questions, please contact our Office assistant, Missy Pody at mapody@seattleschools.org
Room Parent

Room parents help facilitate communication between the teacher and families. In addition, they collaborate with the teacher for various celebrations and activities throughout the year. If you would like to be a room parent, please contact your child’s classroom teacher or volunteer@montlakepta.org
Classroom Volunteers

Teachers often welcome parent volunteers in their classrooms throughout the year, offering both recurring and one-time commitments. There are also many opportunities throughout the year to chaperone field trips or help with special projects and events in the classroom.
Key Processes and Accounts
Who do I contact if my child is absent?
If your child will be absent, you must email montlake.attendance@seattleschools.org and your child’s teacher. Prompt notification saves our office staff from extraneous administrative tasks.
How do I check my child’s grades and test scores?

Bookmark the SPS website called The Source. This is your first stop for anything related to your child’s school record including grades, test scores, and checked out library books. You will also pay for field trips on this site.
How does my child pay for lunch from the cafeteria?

Children can purchase meals or milk in the cafeteria. You can add money to your child’s account using PayPAMS. To create your account, first visit The Source (your go-to place for anything related to your child’s school record) and note their student ID number.
Breakfast and lunch will be served at no cost to those students who qualify for free or reduced-price meals. More information on Culinary Services.
Enrollment & School Choice
Do you know a neighbor or friend considering Montlake?
Families in the geographic attendance zone for Montlake Elementary should enroll now.

Families zoned to other schools who want to attend Montlake should follow the SPS Open Enrollment for School Choice process. School choice applications are typically due by January 31st, with late applications accepted through March 31st.
